title: Two Years of Organoid Electrophysiology — SUSTech Open Meeting
excerpt: A talk on collecting signals from miniature brains in a dish: from rigid electrodes to MESH-GRIP.
body: How do we record meaningful electrophysiology from organoids that reshape themselves over days? That question guided the narrative of my SUSTech Open Meeting presentation.
I walked through the arc of the project:
• Early rigid approaches — good contact, bad compliance
• Lessons in mechanical mismatch and contact area
The biggest shift was realizing that conformity matters more than conductivity. A perfect electrode that loses contact gives you nothing.
• Rigid (Si/SiO2): Excellent recording, but organoids detach within 24h
• Flexible (PI/PET): Better contact, but creasing causes electrode fracture
• Stretchable (mesh): Conforms to organoid surface, survives cyclic strain

Core Insight
The organoid doesn't care about impedance. It cares about proximity. Get close, stay close.

Feedback from faculty and peers helped sharpen how we explain the why behind flexible bioelectronics to a general technical audience. That clarity feeds back into the paper drafts, so the loop is worth it.
If you can't explain it to a first-year graduate student, you don't understand it well enough.
